subject: Short-term quota uplift & tiered burst safeguard discussion
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@shelfwise.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-08T14:23:00Z
Subject: Request: Short-term quota uplift for Nov campaign

Jordan —

We’re ramping a targeted shop-the-runner test during the first 72 hours of our November promotion and expect peak token volume ~7x our current baseline (estimate attached). We need an emergency plan for a temporary quota increase that doesn’t lock us into a long-term commit. Can you outline options for:

- Short window uplift (48–96h) pricing
- Grace credits or rollbacks if actual usage is lower than forecast
- Contract language around overrun true-ups and invoicing cadence

Also include any SLA/latency assurances you can provide — customer impact here is high and we need operational guarantees. We’re evaluating two vendors; pricing clarity and fast turnaround will be the tie-breaker.

Thanks,
Nora Patel
Head of Platform
Shelfwise

Attachment: shelfwise_usage_snapshot_sep.csv (CSV, 43KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Nora Patel <nora@shelfwise.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-08T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Short-term quota uplift for Nov campaign

Nora —

Thanks for the details and the snapshot; that helps. High-level options we can move on quickly: 

Option A — Short-burst headroom (recommended for one-off spikes)
- Duration: 48–96 hours
- Price: one-time headroom fee = pro-rated equivalent of a 1-week 25% commit + 20% uplift on our standard overage rate for any tokens above the headroom (first 72h).
- Grace: unused headroom can be converted to a one-time credit against the next invoice (valid 60 days).

Option B — Discounted overrun true-up (minimal paperwork, fastest to enable)
- No advance commit; overage billed at 30% discount to published overrun price for the first 72 hours post spike.
- True-up invoice issued within the next billing cycle; can be split across two invoices on request.

Option C — Short-term pro-rated commit
- Pro-rate a 1-month committed tier to cover expected uplift; lower unit price but requires PO/commit.

SLA/credits: for short-burst safety, we can include a conditional SLA credit (service unavailable >5 min in any 15-min window during the uplift -> credit = 10% of the uplift fee, escalatable with engineering owner on call).

I’ve attached a provisional term sheet that maps fees and examples from your usage snapshot. If you want, we can enable Option B immediately and swap to Option A with a signed term sheet within 24 hours.

Next steps I suggest: select Option A or B, confirm max expected tokens (or upper bound), and I’ll route for internal approval for the discounted overrun and a provisional headroom hold.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisional_burst_term_sheet.pdf (PDF, 92KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-09-09T09:14:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: Short-term quota uplift for Nov campaign — approval needed

Laura / Ben —

Forwarding Shelfwise request. Nora asked for the fastest path; she’s leaning to Option B (discounted overrun) because it needs zero PO. My ask: approve a temporary 30% discount to our published overrun rate for the first 72 hours and allow conversion to a headroom credit if they sign a short term sheet within 24 hours.

Rationale: low friction, preserves revenue capture, and likely to convert to commit given their traffic profile. If approved I’ll enable the discount now and draft a quick amendment for signature.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY or comment.

—Jordan

Thanks — Option B works best for us (discounted overrun true-up). Can you confirm:

1) The 30% discounted overrun rate applies only to the first 72 hours of the spike, after which regular overrun pricing applies.
2) True-up invoicing timing: we prefer split invoicing (50% on next bill, remainder on following month) — is that possible?
3) Can you send the amendment/agreement to sign (PO coming from procurement).

We’ll provide a final upper-bound token estimate by Monday EOD to set the soft cap. Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can send the agreement I’ll get procurement to sign asap.
